subject: Rate card request + competitor pricing (OpenAI/Anthropic/Together/AWS)
messages:
From: Jared Lim <jared.lim@acmeai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Rate card request and competitor comparison

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the quick intro yesterday. Procurement at Acme AI would like a baseline hosted API rate card and a simple competitor comparison so we can evaluate total cost of ownership. Specifically we need:

- Per-token generation price (short context) for the top 2-3 models you recommend for a chat assistant workload
- Embeddings price (per-embed) and any volume bands
- Any context-length or request-size surcharges (e.g., >8k tokens)
- Baseline latency SLOs for hosted API and any additional cost for lower-latency tiers
- Typical discounting structure for committed monthly spend (first-year overview)

We also ask that you include a column comparing your published hosted rates to the current market price points we've been quoted from OpenAI, Anthropic, Together, and AWS. Our procurement deadline is tight — ideally a formal quote within 10 business days.

I attached our usage profile (acme_rate_request.xlsx) with expected monthly requests and token mix. Let me know if you want a quick call to walk through it.

Thanks,
Jared Lim
Head of Procurement
Acme AI

[Attachment: acme_rate_request.xlsx (xlsx, 24KB)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jared Lim <jared.lim@acmeai.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Rate card request and competitor comparison

Hi Jared —

Appreciate the detail and the sheet. I pulled together a short summary and attached our latest hosted rate card (redwood_ratecard_v2.pdf). Key points up front: 

- Baseline hosted API rates (public):
  • Generation: $0.0035 / 1k tokens (standard model profile)
  • Embeddings: $0.0020 / embed (up to 10M/mo)
  • Context surcharge: $0.0009 / 1k tokens over 16k context
  • Streaming/low-latency tier add-on: +25% to per-token rate (SLO-backed)

- Discounting (examples):
  • 10% off list for 50k USD/mo commit
  • 18% off list for 150k USD/mo commit
  • Custom pricing for enterprise/Dedicated deployments (we can barter on term + commit)

- Competitor parity: we can consider a targeted match on per-token economics vs OpenAI/Anthropic for hosted usage if Acme commits to a 12-month minimum and shares expected monthly consumption (your sheet helps). Together and AWS are typically competitive at very high volumes — we usually make up the difference via latency/availability and SLOs.

Quick asks from our side:
1) Can you confirm the monthly committed spend range you are targeting (from the sheet we saw 60k-120k USD/mo)?
2) Are embeddings heavily used for search (we price differently for batch embed-heavy workloads)?
3) Any data residency/SLA requirements (affects whether you need Dedicated or Private)?

If that looks good, I recommend a 30-minute pricing alignment call this week so we can fast-follow with a formal quote and optional term sheet.

Thanks — attaching the rate card and a short pricing digest.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0187

[Attachment: redwood_ratecard_v2.pdf (pdf, 112KB)]

From: Jared Lim <jared.lim@acmeai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acmeai.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 08:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Rate card request and competitor comparison

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A few clarifying notes: 

- Yes, our target commit is likely in the 75k-125k USD/mo band; core search embedding volume is significant (~40% tokens are embeddings).
- For benchmarking, we have these target competitor numbers (from recent quotes):
  • OpenAI (gpt-4 style): $0.0030 / 1k tokens (generation)
  • Anthropic: $0.0028 / 1k tokens
  • Together: $0.0022 / 1k tokens at very high volumes
  • AWS: varies but can be as low as $0.0018 / 1k tokens with commit + reserved instances

We're asking Redwood to indicate whether you can meet or get within 10-15% of these per-token numbers for hosted API. If matching requires a Dedicated or Private deployment, flag that and include the incremental cost.

Procurement would like the formal quote and a line-by-line competitor comparison in spreadsheet form (same columns as our sheet). Can you send that by Fri 12 Mar? We also want to see any standard enterprise concessions (e.g., invoice cadence, trial credits, breach/credit terms).

Appreciate the rapid turnaround.

Onwards,
Jared

[Attachment: acme_rate_request_v2.xlsx (xlsx, 28KB)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Sun, 01 Mar 2026 10:20:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Rate card request and competitor comparison

Team — forwarding Acme's ask and their updated sheet. Quick context: they are a strong strategic prospect (ML-first, potential for dedicated capacity in 2027). Procurement is testing price parity against OpenAI/Anthropic/Together/AWS. They expect a formal quote/competitor comparison by 12 Mar.

Specific asks:
- Vivek: can you produce a spreadsheet that copies their columns and shows our list, proposed committed tier price, and an "effective price after discounts" column. Flag where match requires Dedicated or Private (and rough delta).
- Rishi: want to confirm how aggressive we can be on list discounts for a 12-month commit in the 80k-120k USD/mo band. Any non-standard concessions we should offer (SLA credit caps, marketing support, pilot credits)?
- Monica: procurement explicitly asked about invoice cadence and standard enterprise concessions. Also they mentioned legal will want standard redlines — can you note any terms that would block a quick 10-business-day turnaround?

Proposed approach: present a two-tier offer — (A) Hosted parity proposal (conditional on 12-month commit + volume schedule) and (B) Dedicated/Private indicative pricing (for comparison). If we go parity on hosted, prefer to require minimum invoice cadence + auto-renew unless they opt for Dedicated.

Can we aim to have the spreadsheet + draft commercial summary by Tue EOD so I can send to Jared Wed morning? Acme is pushing procurement timelines.

Thanks —
Marissa

[Attachment: acme_rate_request_v2.xlsx (xlsx, 28KB)]

Marissa / team — thanks for flagging. High-level proposal to be sent to Acme (we should convert to a formal quote once they confirm target commit):

1) Hosted parity (conditional):
   - Requirement: 12-month minimum, committed spend: $100k/mo (we can tier 80k - 120k with step discounts)
   - Proposed effective rates after commit (illustrative):
     • Generation: $0.0029 / 1k tokens (matches within ~3% of OpenAI/Anthropic quotes)
     • Embeddings: $0.0019 / embed
     • Context surcharge: $0.00085 / 1k tokens over 16k
   - Conditions: invoice monthly, non-cancellable for 30 days after signing, auto-renew 12-month term

2) Dedicated/Private alternative (if they require firm per-token at large scale):
   - Setup + provisioning estimate (one-time): $120k - $250k depending on regions & redundancy
   - Lower effective per-token economics for very high sustained volume (we'd provide a 20-30% discount vs hosted list)

3) Commercial concessions we can offer to expedite:
   - 4 weeks of pilot credits (applied to first invoice)
   - A capped SLA credit (standard) but no unlimited credits for free — propose 5% credit cap of monthly invoice for SLO misses
   - Co-marketing credit for logos / joint case study (negotiable)

Next steps: Vivek to assemble the competitor spreadsheet (our list vs their columns) and Monica to annotate legal/terms that will be non-starters. Once that’s clean we can produce a formal quote + draft MSA.

Happy to jump on a 30-min call with Acme Wednesday 10:00 AM PT if that helps close the gap.

Best,

VP, Sales — Redwood Inference
